name: @voidcode/desktop
description: Local-first desktop IDE for studying research papers and solving the problems inside them
//type: Deliberately NOT "module". Main and the sandboxed preload must be CommonJS (a sandboxed preload has no ESM loader), and with type:module Node would treat the emitted .js as ESM and fail on require. Source is written as ESM and bundled to CJS by electron-vite; the renderer bundle is ESM but loaded via <script type=module> over app://, so it is unaffected.

scripts.//build:renderer: The Next static export the app:// scheme serves. Separate from `build` because electron-vite does not know about it, and packaging must not be able to run without it.
scripts.smoke: npm run build:renderer && electron-vite build && cross-env VOIDCODE_SMOKE=1 electron out/main/index.js
scripts.//smoke:vision: Asks whether an attached image actually reaches the model, which `smoke` cannot: its consent check runs against a scripted provider, so it passes while the model answers about a picture it never read. Needs Ollama with a vision model; skips cleanly without one.
scripts.smoke:vision: npm run build:renderer && electron-vite build && node scripts/vision-e2e.mjs
scripts.//smoke:account: Registration, sign-in and reset-by-code against the REAL API and a real Postgres, driven through the real app. `smoke` cannot ask this: it sets VOIDCODE_DEV_SESSION_TOKEN, so sessionToken() answers before reading the vault and storeSession never runs. Opt-in, needs VOIDCODE_E2E_DATABASE_URL set explicitly; skips cleanly without it.
scripts.smoke:account: npm run build:renderer && electron-vite build && node scripts/account-e2e.mjs
scripts.//package: Vendors Pyodide first, and that ordering is load-bearing rather than tidy. `desktop/vendor/` is gitignored and `electron-builder.yml` copies `vendor/pyodide-packages` as an extraResource, so packaging a clean clone without it either errors on a missing directory or — with the `*.whl` filter — silently ships an app that reaches for a CDN the first time a learner runs Python. That breaks the offline promise in spec §4.4, and it breaks it in the build a user installs rather than in CI where someone would see it. Cheap to keep: loadPyodide reuses the wheel cache, so a repeat run is a no-op.
scripts.package: npm run vendor:pyodide && npm run collect:licences && npm run build:renderer && electron-vite build && electron-builder --publish never
scripts.//dev:renderer: The renderer in a browser, for design work on the static routes. Replaces `harness`, which pointed a bare Vite server at a `src/renderer` that stopped existing when the renderer became a Next app. Deep links into /problems/{id} and /interviews/{slug} 500 here and only here: `next dev` under `output: export` insists a requested param be listed in generateStaticParams, while the packaged app has no Next server at all and serves any slug through the shell over app://.
scripts.//derive: Print a derived answer key for a newly authored interview problem, or with no id audit every recorded snapshot against what the sandbox produces now. Needs Electron because the sandbox is a utilityProcess; see runDeriveKey in src/main/index.ts.
scripts.derive: electron-vite build && cross-env VOIDCODE_DERIVE= electron out/main/index.js
scripts.//collect:licences: Gathers build/licenses/, which electron-builder copies into the installed app as resources/licenses/. Wired into `package` because the app shipped no licence text at all and NOTICE claimed otherwise: Apache-2.0 s4(d) requires the NOTICE accompany distribution and MPL-2.0 s3.1 requires recipients be given the terms. Pyodide ships no licence file, so its text is committed at build/licences-static/.
scripts.//export:catalogue: Dump the graded catalogue — references, normalise expressions and hidden-case arguments — for the Python reward harness in the training repo. Writes the answer key in plain text; the output belongs in that repo, never in a build.
scripts.//render:icon: Regenerates build/icon.svg and build/icon.png from one set of constants. Both are committed; the raster is what electron-builder derives .ico/.icns from, and the vector is what a reviewer can read.
